source.title: Arabic Safety Alignment as Selective Refusal: An Empirical Study of SFT, DPO, and Guard Calibration

record.tranche_reason: Extends empirical evaluation of post-training effects on refusal behavior to Arabic-capable models and Arabic writing forms. Its SFT examples use refusals as targets for harmful prompts, and its main harmful-prompt metric is refusal—not harmful compliance—so it does not test the claim versions as stated.
record.gate_note: The study reports many SFT operating points, but H is explicitly a refusal rate and its complement is not automatically harmful compliance. Its harmful-prompt SFT targets are refusals, not harmful completions. These measurements therefore cannot establish that fine-tuning causes harmful compliance. The study does not measure per-token KL, compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or localization in weights/ranks. It reports direction separability and direction-threshold operating points, but these do not test parameter localization or why safety would be shallow.
record.test_reason: The study neither tests nor relies on any version. Its SFT pairs harmful prompts with refusal targets, mixed with benign data; no run is harmful-completion or benign-only fine-tuning. Its metric H is refusal, not harmful compliance. There is no per-token KL, prefill, suffix or decoding attack, weight or rank localization, or deepening training. Qi et al. is only cited, for the refusal-only diagnostic and in related work. The reader's 'tests' relation contradicts its own all-'not_tested' version list. T6 with cites_only fits better.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also stress that refusal metrics must stay distinct from harmful-response outcomes, and that guards lower H after SFT for four of five models.
record.recipe_differences: The SFT experiments use translated Arabic harmful prompts with refusal targets, often mixed with benign instruction data; the paper reports refusal rates and operating points rather than harmful-compliance rates. It is an Arabic-setting study, not the original harmful-completion fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, benign/refusal ratio, training stage, checkpoint, and Arabic form. The selected SFT candidate is threshold-sensitive for Fanar across seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed benign/refusal SFT moves the joint benign- and harmful-prompt refusal point; H rises above base in every tested mixture, and the size of the move depends on model and ratio.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Arabic-capable instruct models, mixed SFT with refusal targets raises harmful-prompt refusal, with a model- and ratio-dependent benign over-refusal cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-only SFT drives benign refusal to 80% or more within 10–30 steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Arabic refusal-only SFT rapidly produces near-blanket refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected MSA-trained SFT raises Arabizi harmful-prompt refusal in all five models, but none reaches 90% and three stay below 55%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MSA refusal training transfers only partially to Arabizi.

record.code_released: No public artifact URL is available in the current record; planned release is described.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of The Fourth Arabic Natural Language Processing Conference
record.problems: H is refusal and is not a harmful-compliance measure. Judge accuracy is lower on Arabizi; Wilson intervals condition on automatic labels and do not include judge error. Primary sweeps use seed 42; only selected SFT configurations use three seeds, with exact per-seed rates unavailable. Ratio coverage and exposure are unequal across models, and exact sample counts per ratio are absent. The transformed prompts are synthetic; some transformation details and artifact materials are unavailable.
record.rows_left_out: The full refusal-only checkpoint trajectories (Table 18), extra ALLaM refusal-only checkpoints (Table 19), complete selected-run and seed details, SFT ordering sweeps, DPO/guard operating points, and base cross-form results were not exhaustively rowed. The refusal-only trajectory rows here retain the 5-step values and the first reported points where B reaches or exceeds 80% for each model; omitted intermediate and later checkpoints are in Table 18. These additional measurements do not establish harmful compliance or test the other claim versions.

untested.parts: All of it: no fine-tuning on harmful completions and no harmful-compliance rate; harmful prompts are paired with refusal targets.
All of it: no benign-only fine-tuning; every mixed SFT run includes refusal-target data, and H measures refusal, not compliance.
All of it: no aligned-versus-base per-token KL.
All of it: no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks. Arabizi and dialect prompts are input-form shifts, not opening-token bypasses.
All of it: refusal-direction AUCs are linear probes, not tests of whether few weights or ranks carry safety.

record.verdict_notes: Recommend reclassifying from tests/T3 to cites_only/T6. No verdicts are given because no version is tested. Arditi-style refusal directions appear only as an AUC probe, not a localization test bearing on V5. In the audit, 25 of 44 non-refusing harmful-prompt responses were harmful or enabling. That figure is not tied to any fine-tuning contrast, so it does not bear on V1 or V2.

versions.untested_parts: The study trains on harmful prompts with refusal targets, not harmful examples with harmful completions; it does not measure harmful compliance.
It tests mixtures of benign data and harmful-prompt refusal data, not ordinary or benign-only fine-tuning, and does not measure harmful compliance.
No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass test.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
No test of whether the data or training objective causes first-token shallowness.
No training to spread safety across response tokens or test of whether such deepening holds up.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.problem: The stage is recorded as not stated, but the paper explicitly identifies the Instruct checkpoint.

relation.reason: The paper cites Qi et al. on safety erosion but neither tests nor relies on shallow safety alignment. Its refusal-direction diagnostics do not establish localization in a small set of weights or ranks.

tranche.reason: Refusal-target SFT, DPO, guards and activation diagnostics do not test V1–V7. No harmful-completion or benign-only fine-tuning experiment is reported; H measures refusal, not harmful compliance.

source_check.notes: Table 5 concerns synthetic Arabizi transformations. Wilson intervals condition on automatic judge labels; Arabizi judge accuracy is reported as 77.5%, and non-refusal cannot be equated with harmful compliance.
